Emmet County Recorder
The Emmet County Recorder is a county office responsible for keeping important public records and handling several registration duties in Estherville, Iowa. Its work includes real estate documents, vital records, military discharges, recreational vehicle registrations, hunting and fishing licenses, and passport applications.
Records and Land Management
Created by the First Legislative Assembly of the Territory of Iowa in 1839, the county recorder has a long role in protecting records connected with real estate. Recorded documents help establish ownership information and protect parties involved in property transactions. The office is also a public place for record searches.
Land and records management covers many document types. Deeds, title changes, real estate contracts, mortgages, easements, leases, assignments, releases, liens, powers of attorney, plats, affidavits, trade names, articles of incorporation, and Uniform Commercial Code filings can be recorded.
For many real estate documents, a Declaration of Value and Groundwater Hazard Statement are required when applicable. Recording fees depend on the document and page count. Deeds and similar documents cost $12 for the first page, $5 for each additional page and $5 for each additional parcel when more than one parcel is listed. Other listed recordings generally cost $7 for the first page and $5 for additional pages.
A land record search can be made by the public. Information such as names of buyers and sellers, dates, legal description, document type and scan number or book and page can help identify the requested record. Copies cost $0.50 per page.
Military and vital records
Military discharge papers, including DD214 documents, may be recorded as permanent records. A certified copy requires the original document to be presented for recording. A copy is available without a basic copy fee, while certification costs $5 for the first page and $0.50 for each additional page.
The recorder also keeps vital records. Emmet County birth and death registrations date from 1880, while statewide records are available according to state record periods. Certified copies of birth, death, and marriage records cost $15 each when the applicant proves legal entitlement and provides identification.
Marriage applications are also handled by the office. The application fee is $35. A valid government photo ID is required for the bride, groom, and an adult third party. Iowa has a three business day waiting period before a marriage license and certificate can be issued, although a waiver may be available for an additional fee and judicial approval.
Registrations and Public Licenses
The recorder has duties that reach beyond courthouse records. The office handles several registrations and licenses connected with transportation, outdoor activities, and identification documents.
The main areas:
Boats, snowmobiles, and ATVs, including registrations, titles, transfers, liens, and related fees.
Hunting and fishing licenses, military records, vital records, land documents and passport applications.
Boat registrations are renewed every three years. Renewal normally occurs after January 1 and before April 30 to avoid a penalty. Boats longer than 17 feet generally need a title, with listed exceptions for canoes, kayaks, and inflatable vessels. Snowmobile and ATV registrations are renewed annually and expire on December 31. Their renewal period runs from September 1 through December 31.
The office also issues hunting and fishing licenses. Applicants need identifying information for the person receiving the license, such as a name, date of birth, Social Security number, driver’s license number, or DNR PIN. Residents and nonresidents under 16 can fish without a license. Lifetime hunting and fishing licenses are available for eligible people aged 65 or older.
Office location and contact information
The Emmet County Recorder’s Office is located in the Emmet County Courthouse at 609 1st Avenue North, Suite #7, Estherville, Iowa 51334. The office phone number is 712–362–4115 and the fax number is 712–362–7454. Regular office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday.
Office functions can be grouped as follows:
Recording and maintaining real estate and other legal documents, including land records, liens, and military discharges.
Maintaining and issuing eligible vital records and processing marriage applications.
Registering boats, snowmobiles, and ATVs, while also issuing hunting and fishing licenses.
Accepting passport applications and providing related document information.
The Recorder’s Office therefore connects several types of county records with everyday legal and administrative matters. Its records provide historical and current information about property, family events, military service, and local county public registrations. Requirements, fees, and state rules can change, so the county’s official information is the appropriate reference for current details.
